title: Two pink flowers: what grows?
hook: Cross two pink flowers. What colours do their seeds grow?

knows: a seed gets one copy of a gene from each parent
doesNotKnow: that some traits blend, so a cross of two blends gives red, pink and white at 1 : 2 : 1

misconception: Pink x pink gives all pink; red and white never come back.
objective: The learner can explain that two pink (R W) parents each pass R or W with equal chance, giving red, pink and white seeds at 1 : 2 : 1, so half are pink.

claims.text: In incomplete dominance the heterozygote looks in between the two homozygotes (a red x white cross gives pink, as in snapdragons).
claims.source: Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis, ch. 6 (incomplete dominance; snapdragon flower colour). The lesson's flower is invented.

claims.text: Two R W parents give seeds R R, R W, W R, W W with equal chance: red 1, pink 2, white 1 out of 4, so half the seeds are pink.
claims.source: Enumeration of the 4 equally likely allele pairs (Mendelian segregation).

claims.text: In the 100 seeded seeds the stage fills, 27 are red, 51 pink and 22 white.
claims.source: Demo.tsx, mulberry32 seed 1, each seed takes one random copy from each R W parent. Seed 1 was the first tried and was not tuned (seeds 2 and 3 give 21/55/24 and 23/49/28 red/pink/white). artifacts/scratch/w5life/pink.mjs.

claims.text: Model (stated on the stage): a made-up flower with one gene, R giving red and W giving white, pink for one of each; each parent passes either copy with equal chance.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #48.

recall.question: A flower is pink when it has one red copy and one white copy of a gene. Cross two pink flowers. About what share of the seeds are pink?
recall.why: Each parent passes red or white with equal chance, giving red, pink and white seeds at 1 : 2 : 1, so half are pink.
